results.title: Struggling and Thriving: Effectuation in Social and Economic Stress
results.content: The aim is to provide a snapshot of some of the most exciting work published in the various research areas of the journal. We used an online survey and collected data from 1014 citizens in Iran to investigate how an effectual logic of thinking as a psychological framework enables some citizens of a non-Western country to address the uncertainties caused by international economic sanctions and sustain their well-being. This study contributes to the multifactorial view of quality of life as well as effectuation theory and enhances our understanding of social sustainability and how it can be cultivated. This study falls within the developmental sustainability school of thought and contributes to sustainability research by applying effectuation theory to understand resilient citizens decision-making under the uncertainty of their daily lives [5] and the outcome in terms of satisfaction with life, unlike the abundance of research on the negative impacts of economic sanctions on society [8].

results.title: A logic of entrepreneurial action without judgment? Effectuation ...
results.content: # A logic of entrepreneurial action without judgment? One such case is its relationship to entrepreneurial judgment, the importance of which for effectuation has been explicitly denied. We revisit this claim and reevaluate whether effectuation can really get by without entrepreneurial judgment. We find that characterizing effectuation as a distinct entrepreneurial logic devoid of judgment is untenable: quite the opposite is true. Effectuation is in fact a specific form of entrepreneurial judgment. Recognizing this helps both to enrich effectuation theory and its practice by incorporating core insights from entrepreneurial judgment theory and to integrate different accounts of entrepreneurial action in attempts to build a more unified entrepreneurial action theory.
